title: Supremum in the extended natural numbers
statement: Let $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ be the set $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ with one element $\infty$ adjoined, totally ordered by the usual order on $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $n<\infty$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Every subset $S\subseteq\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ has a supremum (least upper bound) $\sup S$, with $\sup\varnothing=0$: if $S\subseteq\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ is bounded, $\sup S$ is its largest element (or $0$ if $S$ is empty); otherwise $\sup S=\infty$. In particular $\sup S$ is finite if and only if there is $R\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ with $s\leq R$ for all $s\in S$.
